extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's The Rising Sea)
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter excerpt giving definitions, characterizations, and criteria for flatness of modules, sheaves, and morphisms; includes examples, exercises, and applications (e.g., base change, flat limits, behavior over special rings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat A-module
rubrics_metrics.description: We say that M is a flat A-module (or flat over A or A-flat) if M ⊗A · is an exact functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently tensoring with M preserves all short exact sequences. This is the basic algebraic definition used throughout; see Exercises and observations in §24.2 for consequences and tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key examples of flat modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Free A-modules (even of infinite rank) are clearly flat. More generally, projective modules are flat. Localizations are flat: if S is multiplicative subset then A → S^{-1}A is flat because localization is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these as basic positive tests; many constructions reduce to these cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat modules are torsion-free (Observation 24.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a non-zerodivisor of A and M is a flat A-module, then multiplication by x on M is injective; in particular flat modules are torsion-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an easy way to show a module is not flat: find torsion. Used repeatedly as a quick negative test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalk/prime-local property of flatness (Proposition 24.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat iff Mp is a flat Ap-module for all prime ideals p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus flatness can be checked locally on primes (or on an affine open cover for schemes). The proof uses localization and behavior of Tor upon localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat quasicoherent sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasicoherent sheaf F on a scheme X is flat at p if F_p is a flat O_{X,p}-module. F is flat (over X) if it is flat at all p ∈ X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By Proposition 24.2.3 this can be checked on an affine open cover; see Definition 24.2.5 and related exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat morphism of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π: X → Y is flat at p if O_{X,p} is a flat O_{Y,π(p)}-module. The morphism is flat if it is flat at all p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the scheme-theoretic extension of module flatness. Check locally on source and target (Definition 24.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat over a base (sheaf over base)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π: X → Y and a quasicoherent sheaf F on X, F is flat over Y at p if F_p is a flat O_{Y,π(p)}-module; F is flat over Y if flat at all p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This unifies the notions F=O_X and X=Y special cases and is used for families and deformation-theoretic statements (Definition 24.2.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a flat B-module and A is a B-algebra, then M ⊗B A is a flat A-module. For morphisms and sheaves, flatness is preserved under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercises 24.2.C and 24.2.I. Important for forming products over fields (e.g., X×_k Y' is flat over Y').

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity of flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a flat B-algebra and M is A-flat, then M is also B-flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to descend flatness along a chain of ring maps (Exercise 24.2.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology commutes with flat base change (Theorem 24.2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Cartesian square with π quasicompact and separated and ρ flat, for any quasicoherent F on X the natural morphisms ρ^*(R^i π_* F) → R^i π'_* (ρ'^* F) are isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases include affine base change (Exercise 18.8.B(b)). This is a fundamental compatibility used to relate cohomology of fibers to higher pushforwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of closed subschemes under flat morphisms preserves ideal sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If X→Z and Y→Z and V⊂X is a closed subscheme, then under flatness hypotheses (e.g., β flat or V flat over Z) the pullback of the ideal sheaf satisfies α^* I_{V/X} ≅ I_{Y×_Z V / Y×_Z X}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §24.2.9 and Exercise 24.3.H. In particular, pullback of ideal sheaf as a quasicoherent sheaf agrees with pullback as closed subschemes in flat situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat maps send associated points to associated points (Exercise 24.2.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X→Y is flat (and locally Noetherian), then any associated point of X maps to an associated point of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives geometric intuition and is used to construct non-flat examples by checking failure of this property (Exercises 24.2.K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal-theoretic criterion for flatness (Theorem 24.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat iff Tor^A_1(M, A/I) = 0 for every ideal I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently the natural map I ⊗_A M → IM is injective (or an isomorphism). This refines the Tor-characterization and is the basis for many concrete checks and classification results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equational criterion for flatness (Exercise 24.4.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: M is flat iff for every relation ∑ a_i m_i = 0 with a_i ∈ A and m_i ∈ M there exist m'_j ∈ M and a_{ij} ∈ A such that m_i = ∑_j a_{ij} m'_j and ∑_i a_i a_{ij} = 0 for all j (i.e., the relation 'comes from' relations in A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an explicit 'linear algebra' style test for flatness; useful for checking when relations in M are induced by relations in A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient to check finitely generated ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: In Theorem 24.4.1 it suffices to check Tor_1(M, A/I) = 0 for finitely generated ideals I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: any ideal is union of finitely generated subideals and Tor commutes with filtered colimits; see Remark 24.4.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat = torsion-free for modules over a PID (Exercise 24.4.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A module over a principal ideal domain is flat if and only if it is torsion-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ideal-theoretic criterion and structure theory for modules over a PID to check flatness concrete examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness over a DVR (Exercise 24.4.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer t, then an A-module M is flat iff t is not a zerodivisor on M, i.e., (M : t) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields a geometric criterion for flatness of families over regular curves (see §24.4.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness over the dual numbers (Exercise 24.4.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A = k[t]/(t^2), M is flat over A iff the multiplication-by-t map M/tM → tM is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concrete criterion is used in deformation theory and has only three ideals to check; helpful for small-nilpotent-thickening examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat = free = projective for finitely presented modules over local rings (Theorem 24.4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m) is a local ring and M is a finitely presented A-module, then M is flat iff it is free iff it is projective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Nakayama's lemma and finite presentation to show kernel vanishes. Corollary: finitely presented sheaf is flat iff locally free (Corollary 24.4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite flat morphisms have locally constant degree (Remark and Exercise 24.4.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X→Y is finite and Y is reduced and locally Noetherian, then π_* O_X is locally free iff its rank (degree) as a function on Y is locally constant — equivalently degree is constant on connected components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this criterion to determine degree of finite flat maps and to rule out non-flat normalizations (Exercise 24.4.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for flatness over a regular curve (Exercise 24.4.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X→Y with Y a regular (locally Noetherian) curve and X locally Noetherian, then π is flat iff all associated points of X map to a generic point of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a geometric and visual criterion for flatness in dimension 1; used to deduce constancy of degrees and to construct flat limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuative criterion for flatness (Unimportant remark 24.4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X→Y is finitely presented then flatness implies for every map Spec DVR → Y, the base change X×_Y Spec DVR has no associated points mapping to the closed point. If Y is reduced and locally Noetherian, this condition is also sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a way to check flatness by testing one-parameter families (DVRs). Reducedness is necessary in the stated sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat limits (24.4.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A a DVR with generic point η and closed point 0, if X is locally Noetherian over A and Y ⊂ X|_η is a closed subscheme, then the scheme-theoretic closure Y' of Y in X is flat over A (the 'flat limit' of Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes taking flat closures in one-parameter degenerations and is often used in degeneration/compactification arguments.
